summary.headline: Orient Bell H1 FY27 revenue grew 18.1% with Q2 EBITDA margin of 9.8%, driven by ~18% volume growth and ~18-20% price increases.
summary.overview: Orient Bell reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 results, with Q2 revenue growth of 14.6% and H1 growth of 18.1%, which management described as industry-leading. Management attributed growth to a secondary-sales focus, digital tools for dealers, and price increases taken from July, while cutting credit in the market. Profitability improved sharply, with Q2 PBT of Rs 16.4 crore (up 326%) and EBITDA margin of about 9.8%, and the working capital cycle fell to 18 days from 20 days in March 2026. Capacity utilisation reached 75% in Q2 after conversion of 1.2 million sq m of ceramic capacity to GVT in October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 740 crore (as stated in transcript, 'stood at 40 crores' unclear)

segments.name: GVT (glazed vitrified tiles)
segments.commentary: GVT share of sales rose to about 45% currently from roughly 20% in FY22-23, after conversion of 1.2 million sq m ceramic capacity to GVT completed in October 2026.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North and Central ~49% of sales, East ~24%; management plans to expand presence in South via TV advertising in Tamil and Kannada and new shop-in-shop displays.

segments.name: Retail vs project mix
segments.commentary: Retail vs project split held at about 80:20; projects defined as sales above 3,000 sq m per quarter.

segments.name: Master Bond (adhesives) and new products
segments.commentary: Anti-static, foldable tiles and tile adhesive (Master Bond) are early-stage, differentiation-focused; Master Bond dispatched from four locations, with expected sales of Rs 3-5 crore per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give formal Q3/Q4 guidance but said double-digit EBITDA margin is expected in H2, with H2 historically stronger than H1.
Gas prices: November 2026 expected to stay at about Rs 83 per unit; December uncertain.
FY27 capex about Rs 20 crore including maintenance; next-year capex plan to be decided in the coming months.
Plans to open new exclusive showrooms starting H2 FY27; about 238-240 touchpoints currently active, with about 200 more shop-in-shop formats planned.
capex_capacity: Conversion of 1.2 million sq m ceramic capacity into GVT completed in October 2026; capacity utilisation 75% in Q2.
Invested about Rs 1.1 crore for 1 MW renewable energy capacity at Dora facility, now powering utilities with green energy.
Management said further ceramic-to-GVT conversion is unlikely; future capacity additions will be new lines.
Own manufacturing gross margin about 38-39%, with Dora expected to be similar within about 1%.
demand_pricing: Volume growth about 15-18% in H1 versus industry volume growth of about 1% excluding OBL; management says market share improved (listed-player share small, industry dominated by unorganised).
Average selling price up about Rs 12 per sq m QoQ (Q2 about Rs 333 vs Q1 about Rs 321); price increases of roughly 18-20% in aggregate, with the last hike in July 2026.
Industry volatility from gas prices; management said 40-50% of manufacturers were shut and may stay closed through November, which could limit further price cuts.
Credit in the market reduced while growing; large low-margin projects declined in favour of mid and small projects.

qa_highlights.question: Geographical split of revenue and plans for the South?
qa_highlights.answer: North and Central 49%, East 24%. Management is building South presence via TV ads in Tamil and Kannada and dealer shop-in-shop displays, with exclusive showrooms to follow in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Current price hike status and whether prices are sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Last hike in July; Q2 average selling price up about Rs 12 QoQ to about Rs 333. Management said further price cuts are unlikely given closures among competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs price contribution to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% volume and about 20% price contribution cited for the quarter, per management's breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is needed to reach double-digit EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 margin was 9.8%; management expects double-digit margin in H2 by staying on execution priorities and said gas price declines would be passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Progress of new products (anti-static, foldable tiles, Master Bond adhesive)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet significant contributors; mainly differentiation tools. Master Bond expected to contribute Rs 3-5 crore per quarter, leveraging dealer network.

qa_highlights.question: Capex strategy and further GVT conversions?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 20 crore capex for FY27 including maintenance; no further ceramic-to-GVT conversions planned; future capex plan to be finalised in next few months.

risks_watch: Gas price volatility and its pass-through to pricing; November at about Rs 83 and December uncertain.
Sustainability of 18-20% price increases if industry supply returns post-Diwali.
Dealer churn in exclusive showrooms, which management says it is working to arrest before expanding.
Limited South India dealer penetration versus competitors, which management did not address in detail.
Pace of Master Bond and new product adoption, still early stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin trajectory, with management stating Q2 EBITDA of 9.8% and H2 double-digit margin expectation. Cautious and non-committal on forward guidance, on gas price outlook and on dealer-specific questions, which were declined.
key_quotes: The reason that we have got these good results is because as I said in my opening statement, we have successfully driven the strategy of secondary sale focus.
So we are almost there. I think quarter two was 9.8 percent this thing.
We went slow on making new boutiques, new showrooms till we fixed the reasons because of which churn was high.

adds.what: Conversion of 1.2 million sq m ceramic capacity to GVT (completed Oct 2026; conversion, not new capacity, and no further conversions planned)
1 MW renewable energy capacity at Dora facility (utilities power, not production capacity)
New exclusive showrooms from H2 FY27, plus ~200 planned shop-in-shop formats (retail touchpoints)

growth.why: Management declined formal Q3/Q4 revenue guidance but expects double-digit EBITDA margin in H2 FY27 (vs 9.8% Q2), backed by price hikes of ~18-20% (last in July 2026), ~18% H1 volume growth against ~1% industry, and 75% utilisation after GVT conversion, with no new ceramic-to-GVT conversions planned and FY27 capex of about Rs 20 crore including maintenance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 9.8% and management expects double-digit EBITDA margin in H2 FY27, backed by ~18-20% price hikes (last in July 2026) and gas-price pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 1.2 million sq m ceramic-to-GVT conversion is already done (Oct 2026) and management said no further conversions are planned; utilisation of 75% leaves headroom, and only new lines would add capacity later with no date given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 volume grew about 15-18% against industry volume growth of about 1% excluding OBL, and share gains are being pursued via dealer digital tools and shop-in-shop displays.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 75% (below the 80% threshold) and FY27 capex is about Rs 20 crore including maintenance; the next-year capex plan is pending and to be decided in the coming months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined formal Q3/Q4 guidance, but H1 revenue grew 18.1% and H2 is historically stronger than H1, so there is room to beat if pricing holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Price increases of ~18-20% could reverse if industry supply returns after Diwali, and gas prices are uncertain beyond November at about Rs 83 per unit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Master Bond adhesive is already dispatched from four locations with expected sales of Rs 3-5 crore per quarter; anti-static and foldable tiles are early-stage and not yet significant.

rows.label: South India push via TV ads and shop-in-shop
rows.why: Management is building South presence with TV ads in Tamil and Kannada, ~200 planned shop-in-shop formats and exclusive showrooms from H2, though North and Central still make up 49% of sales and South dealer penetration is limited.

rows.label: Price sustainability of 18-20% hikes
rows.why: Average selling price rose about Rs 12 per sq m QoQ to about Rs 333, and management says competitor closures (40-50% of manufacturers shut through November) make further price cuts unlikely, but the hikes depend on supply staying tight.

rows.label: Working capital cycle at 18 days
rows.why: The cycle fell to 18 days from 20 days in March 2026 as credit to the market was cut, and this could hold or improve further, though the brief gives no target.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth (H1 revenue +18.1%), margin trajectory (Q2 EBITDA 9.8%, double-digit in H2) and share gains, but declined formal Q3/Q4 guidance, gas-price outlook and dealer-specific questions; the brief does not show detailed analyst pushback.
